headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: RD-Agent’s broad API/browser egress can expose Rasa outputs, while shared-output workflows create prompt-injection and capability-conflict exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Rasa can ingest text/voice from chat channels, and RD-Agent can browse and call external APIs, so a shared handoff path could let attacker-controlled content in RD-Agent outputs influence Rasa if operators bridge them. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and uncertainty pushes severity up from low.
conditions: IF an operator copies RD-Agent-generated text into a Rasa intent, response, or knowledge source
IF both agents are connected through a shared file, chat, or ticketing channel
mitigations: Disable copy-paste handoffs between agents
Require human review of RD-Agent outputs before feeding Rasa
Strip instructions from any imported text
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Rasa handles text and voice, while RD-Agent touches financial reports, research papers, execution traces, logs, and secrets, and it has broad network egress plus API access. If Rasa outputs or user data are forwarded into RD-Agent, sensitive content can leave the local boundary through third-party APIs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default docs-driven workflows.
conditions: IF Rasa transcripts or voice-derived text are forwarded into RD-Agent prompts or logs
IF RD-Agent sends those prompts to OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek, or Kaggle APIs
mitigations: Do not route customer-support transcripts into RD-Agent
Redact secrets and personal data before any RD-Agent call
Restrict RD-Agent egress to approved endpoints only
Separate credentials for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on inter-agent payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Rasa is not multi-instance capable, while RD-Agent supports multiple instances and writes logs/files. If both are pointed at the same workspace or log directory, concurrent writes can corrupt state or overwrite artifacts. The profiles do not prove a shared directory, so the conflict is real but not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path or log directory
IF an orchestrator launches parallel RD-Agent instances alongside a single Rasa workspace
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run only one writer per workspace
Lock shared files during writes
Keep Rasa and RD-Agent in separate containers
requires-engineering: add filesystem locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent can consume external content and produce research outputs, and Rasa can surface those outputs in conversations. If Rasa treats RD-Agent text as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into user-facing responses or downstream actions. The pairwise chain is plausible, but no direct automation from Rasa to action-taking is documented.
conditions: IF RD-Agent outputs are inserted into Rasa responses without validation
IF Rasa is configured to answer users from RD-Agent-generated summaries
mitigations: Add a verification step before Rasa uses RD-Agent output
Require citations for any generated factual claim
Limit RD-Agent output to drafts only
Review high-impact responses manually
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating on handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles secrets and data classes like financial reports and logs, while Rasa handles customer-support text and voice. If customer-support data includes regulated personal data and is forwarded into RD-Agent’s third-party APIs, retention or residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify jurisdictions, so this is a compliance-risk inference rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF customer-support transcripts contain regulated personal data
IF those transcripts are sent from Rasa into RD-Agent-hosted third-party APIs or logs
mitigations: Classify data before handoff
Block regulated data from RD-Agent inputs
Review retention settings for both agents
Use separate storage policies per agent
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement
